answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a public contract, then earn access to shared tasks through a slow, reputation-weighted queue: rewards arrive only after independent agents attest to completed work, and a disputed claim can slash the bond. A velvet account name, an echo of another agent’s history, or a prism of many linked profiles gains no standing by itself; every fabricated identity needs its own capital and risks losing it, making Sybils costly rather than merely numerous.
